story.title: Tiger Woods Changes Plea in DUI Case, License Suspended for Five Years
story.summary: Tiger Woods appeared in a Florida court to change his plea in a DUI case stemming from a rollover crash. As part of a plea deal, he will have his driver's license suspended for five years.

timeline_highlights.title: Tiger Woods Enters Plea Deal for Reckless Driving Charge Following Florida Crash
timeline_highlights.summary: Tiger Woods has pleaded no contest to a reckless driving charge related to a rollover crash in Florida earlier this year. As part of a plea agreement, he will face a five-year driving ban and a $1,000 fine. The incident reportedly occurred while Woods was distracted by his phone and adjusting the radio.

event_overview.title: About Tiger Woods Incident
event_overview.subject: Tiger Woods Incident
event_overview.summary: This event concerns the criminal case arising from Tiger Woods’ March 27, 2026 rollover crash on Jupiter Island in Martin County, Florida. Authorities initially alleged DUI-related offenses; the case was later resolved in Martin County court through an amended reckless-driving disposition rather than a trial on the original DUI allegation.

facts.label: Incident date and location
facts.value: The crash occurred on March 27, 2026, on Jupiter Island in Martin County, Florida, after Woods’ Land Rover collided with a trailer and rolled onto its side.

facts.label: Initial allegations
facts.value: Woods initially faced misdemeanor allegations of driving under the influence with property damage and refusing to submit to a lawful test; he entered a not-guilty plea before the case was amended.

facts.label: Court resolution
facts.value: On September 2, 2026, Woods pleaded no contest to an amended reckless-driving charge in Martin County, resolving the criminal case without a trial on the original DUI charge.

facts.label: Driving privilege consequence
facts.value: The court ordered a five-year driver-license suspension as part of the disposition. Separately, Florida law authorizes administrative license suspension when a driver refuses a lawful breath, blood, or urine test; that administrative process is distinct from the criminal case outcome.

facts.label: Court and records access
facts.value: The case was handled in Martin County, whose Clerk of Court maintains court-record access and processes public-records requests for records in its custody.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the September 2, 2026 plea-related developments, not the complete crash investigation, evidentiary record, medical-treatment history, or every prior driving-related incident involving Woods.

related_stories.title: Former Madagascar Senate President Sentenced for Role in Protest Violence
related_stories.summary: Richard Ravalomanana, the former Senate president of Madagascar, has been sentenced to 10 years of hard labor after being found guilty of complicity in murder related to a violent crackdown on youth-led protests last year. The unrest resulted in at least 22 fatalities and over 100 injuries, as reported by the UN.

related_stories.title: Nepal Faces Mass Burials as Flash Flood Death Toll Surpasses 1,100
related_stories.summary: In Nepal, mass burials of unidentified victims are ongoing as the death toll from recent flash floods exceeds 1,100. The government's decision to conduct temporary burials has sparked outrage among the largely Hindu population, who argue that this practice contradicts their religious traditions.

related_stories.title: USS Abraham Lincoln Arrives in Thailand After Extended Deployment
related_stories.summary: The USS Abraham Lincoln aircraft carrier has arrived in eastern Thailand after more than nine months at sea, primarily spent in the Middle East. Reports have emerged regarding challenging conditions on board, including food shortages and plumbing issues, prompting calls from some lawmakers for an investigation into the deployment's impact on crew welfare.
